provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: There is no formal quality assessment (risk of bias) screening of included studies, so the reader cannot judge whether the meta-analysis is built on biased or erroneous data that could perpetuate mis-estimation. Key study features such as population, recruitment, attrition, power, and measure validity are unreported.
issues.quote: The most serious concern I have is that there is no formal quality assessment (risk of bias) screening. Without this, we have no sense of whether or not this meta-analysis perpetuates the 'trash in - trash out' problem

issues.text: The choice of control variables is discussed very briefly and is not theoretically motivated. SES may be a confounder and also an effect modifier of lead's neurotoxicity, so inappropriate modeling of SES and other controls could bias estimates of lead effects or misattribute effects to other risk factors.
issues.quote: the choice of controls is discussed very briefly and is not theoretically motivated for the reader. For instance, SES could be not only a confounder but could modify the neurotoxic effects of lead exposure.

issues.text: Overall, given the lack of quality assessment, the unmotivated controls, and questions about timepoint inclusion, the evaluator does not take the evidence base in the review as causal, noting that most of the data is observational.
issues.quote: I do not personally take the evidence base captured in the review as causal. Most of the data is observational as well.

issues.text: The inclusion criterion requiring blood lead measured from the same individuals at different times is ambiguous; it is unclear whether blood lead must be measured before the cognitive or achievement outcome.
issues.quote: I assume if different time points, it would still be required that blood lead level is measured before IQ/ reading/ math, though I cannot find whether this was the specific inclusion criterion

issues.text: The extraction rule covers maternal as well as child blood lead levels, but maternal lead is not mentioned again. It is unclear whether no studies used maternal measures or whether maternal and child lead were treated the same, which the evaluator would find concerning without justification.
issues.quote: there is no further mention of maternal lead beyond p.6, does this mean no studies used maternal measures or whether lead at the maternal or child level was treated the same?

issues.text: The exclusion of results with blood measures at multiple ages appears unjustified, since the first available age would seem comparable to other included studies meeting the timing criteria.
issues.quote: this sounds strange to me, given that likely the first available age would be comparable to all other included studies

issues.text: The review is non-systematic but the authors searched only Google Scholar, which is a search engine rather than a systematic database. The evaluator argues that its results are non-replicable and cannot be screened systematically, so using 'systematic review' terminology is misleading. Non-systematic search also means relevant studies could have been missed or selected in a biased way.
issues.quote: The authors searched only in Google Scholar - this is not a systematic search database but simply a search engine, and I think it's deeply misleading to use the terminology of 'systematic review' in such cases.

issues.text: The reported number of search results (951 potential results) cannot be reproduced; the evaluator's replication returned about 9.3 million results, and the evaluation manager also got many more results than reported, implying an undisclosed arbitrary stopping rule.
issues.quote: when I try to replicate the authors' search strategy in section 2.1 the output I get from GS is "About 9,330,000 results" so it's very difficult for me to understand how the authors report that they "found 951 potential results"

issues.text: The specification curve is not implemented in a principled way; controls could be reported stepwise and subsamples could compare high-income and LMIC studies more directly.
issues.quote: Specification curve - minor; perhaps could have been done in a more principled way - e.g. controls reported in stepwise manner (first each on their own, then combined)

issues.text: Corrected-for-publication-bias pooled effects are described only qualitatively; the evaluator wants the numeric corrected effect reported in the paper.
issues.quote: (Though I do wish this corrected-for-publication-bias effect (based on either method) would be provided in numeric terms in the report.)

issues.text: Most of the included studies (29 of 47) come from high-income countries, suggesting a need for more data from LMICs, though the evaluator notes this cannot be a strong claim given the non-systematic approach.
issues.quote: from the 47s studies, 29 are in high income countries, which might suggest need for more data in LMICs

issues.text: Figure labels need improvement; for example, effect type should be stated directly in the label.
issues.quote: some figures need better labeling, e.g. include effect type directly in label.

issues.text: The report does not follow reporting standards such as PRISMA, including inter-rater reliability measures, which the evaluator notes as a standard the review is held to only partly.
issues.quote: reporting standards such as inter-rater reliability measures - see PRISMA reporting standards for me
